x: When the competitors did come along, Penny was nearly hundred yards ahead of Ginty and he in turn was about the same distance in front of a hot little trio consisting of Footer, Allum and Carter, followed a little later by Ring and Shields.

Jim Ginty was fourth at this point, and our other men all seemed to be weighing up their opponents and running strongly. An attempt to get an idea of the scoring was doomed to failure owing to the speed with which the men passed.
Footer, Ginty and Carter were especially prominent of ours. Returning from the first lap our good start had gone, but we were well placed with Surrey A.C. looking very dangerous.
We hope to fare well in the four remaining events and repeat our win of last year in the League. The men to represent us were: 3 miles, Ring (4); Carter (7); Allum (10); Ginty (11): and 440 yards, R.

At the same meeting Jim Ginty essayed his first attempt at the Two Miles Steeplechase (Southern Championship), and ran so well that he forced the A.A.A. and Southern Counties champion to run much faster than he did in last years A.A.A. championship.

In our last issue we had occasion to refer to the scandalous way in which Jim Ginty has been ignored when the England team to meet France was selected; and expressed the hope that some enquiries should be instituted, and an attempt made to secure some satisfaction.

Patience abroad on Foreign service we knew things would be more difficult, but with Ginty unable to run owing to ankle trouble, and Saunders arriving late following a motor-cycle breakdown, Cadogan A.C. were certainly up against it!
Twelve months ago these columns recorded our indignation at the non-selection of Jim Ginty as a member of the English International team, after he had so clearly demonstrated his claims in the A.A.A.
At the half-way mark Penny and Ginty were leading with Parker about 30 yards behind. At this point fifteen runners passed within a minute of the leaders—a very satisfactory state of affairs.
Taylor, and, most unfortunately, Jim Ginty was also unable to help our team.

With such names as Penny, Footer, Ginty, Parker, D. Patience, Carter and Cohen to think of, it will be seen that we have every chance of success to bring the title where it has so seldom been in late years, namely the South.
